```{r}
#| results: hide
#| message: false

library(data.table)
library(echarts4r)

BridgeData <- fread("BridgeData.csv")
CofogName <- fread("cofog-kod-nev.csv")

# Categories of one classification that are the sum of categories of the other,
# by their codes: those of COFOG (GF...) are made of Hungarian ones (F...), and
# vice versa
aggregates <- list(
  GF01 = c("F01", "F15"),
  GF0101 = c("F01.a", "F01.b", "F01.c"),
  GF0104 = c("F01.d", "F01.e"),
  GF04 = c("F09", "F10", "F11", "F12", "F13"),
  F01 = c("GF0101", "GF0102", "GF0103", "GF0104", "GF0105", "GF0106"),
  F01.f = c("GF0102", "GF0103", "GF0105", "GF0106"),
  F03.b = c("GF0301", "GF0305", "GF0306"),
  F04.d = c("GF0905", "GF0906", "GF0907", "GF0908")
)

# The rows to add to `data` for the aggregates made of the codes in its column
# `from` ("huncode" or "cofog"): for each year and type, the sum of the parts,
# coded only in the other column
aggregate_rows <- function(data, from) {
  to <- setdiff(c("huncode", "cofog"), from)
  codes <- names(aggregates)[startsWith(names(aggregates), "GF") == (from == "huncode")]
  rbindlist(lapply(codes, \(code) {
    parts <- aggregates[[code]]
    # A misspelt code would otherwise just be left out of the sum
    absent <- setdiff(parts, data[[from]])
    if (length(absent) > 0) stop(code, ": no data for ", toString(absent))
    rows <- data[get(from) %chin% parts, .(value = sum(value)), by = .(year, type)]
    rows[, (c(to, from, "level")) := list(
      code, NA_character_, if (grepl("^G?F[0-9]{2}$", code)) "main_group" else "subgroup"
    )]
  }))
}

HunData <- readRDS(url("https://github.com/ferenci-tamas/magyar-koltsegvetes-adatbazis/raw/refs/heads/main/magyar-koltsegvetes-funkcionalis-kiadasok.rds"))
HunData <- rbind(

             huncode = "F01.e", hunname = "Műszaki fejlesztés",
             column = c("2015. évi teljesítés", "2016. évi eredeti előirányzat",
                        "2016. évi törvényi módosított", "2016. évi teljesítés"),
             year = c(2015, 2016, 2016, 2016),
             type = c("actual", "original_plan", "modified_plan", "actual"),
             value = 0),
  data.table(doc_year = 2027, doc_type = "Tervezet", row = 7, level = "subgroup",
             huncode = "F01.e", hunname = "Műszaki fejlesztés",
             column = "2027. évi előirányzat", year = 2027,
             type = "original_plan", value = 0)
)

HunName <- unique(HunData[level %notin% c("total", "function"), .(hunMagyar = hunname, huncode)])

HunData <- rbind(
  HunData[doc_type == "Zarszamadas" & type == "original_plan" & year == doc_year & level %notin% c("total", "function"), .(year, type, level, huncode, value)],
  HunData[year == 2025 & type == "original_plan" & year == doc_year & level %notin% c("total", "function"), .(year, type, level, huncode, value)],
  HunData[year == 2026 & type == "original_plan" & year == doc_year & level %notin% c("total", "function"), .(year, type, level, huncode, value)],
  HunData[year == 2027 & type == "original_plan" & year == doc_year & level %notin% c("total", "function"), .(year, type, level, huncode, value)],
  HunData[doc_type == "Zarszamadas" & type == "actual" & year == doc_year & level %notin% c("total", "function"), .(year, type, level, huncode, value)],
  HunData[doc_type == "Zarszamadas" & type == "actual" & year == 2002 & level %notin% c("total", "function"), .(year, type, level, huncode, value)]
)
# HunData[is.na(value)]
HunData[is.na(value) & huncode == "F01.e", value := 0]

HunData <- merge(HunData, BridgeData, by = "huncode", sort = FALSE, all.x = TRUE)

HunData <- rbind(HunData, aggregate_rows(HunData, from = "huncode"))

HunData <- merge(HunData, HunData[!is.na(huncode) & level == "main_group", .(total = sum(value)), .(year, type)],
                 by = c("year", "type"), sort = FALSE)
HunData$huncodeParent <- substring(HunData$huncode, 1, 3)
HunData$cofogParent <- substring(HunData$cofog, 1, 4)

HunData <- merge(HunData, HunData[!is.na(huncode) & level == "main_group", .(totalParent = value, year, type, huncodeParent)],
                 by = c("year", "type", "huncodeParent"), sort = FALSE, all.x = TRUE)

ESData <- data.table(eurostat::get_eurostat("gov_10a_exp", filters = list(geo = "HU"), cache = FALSE))
saveRDS(ESData, "ESData.rds")
ESData <- ESData[freq == "A" & unit == "MIO_NAC" & sector == "S13" & na_item == "TE" & geo == "HU" & cofog99 != "TOTAL" & !is.na(values),
                 .(cofog = cofog99, year = lubridate::year(time), type = "actual_cofog", value = values)]

ESData$level <- ifelse(nchar(ESData$cofog) == 4, "main_group", "subgroup")

ESData <- rbind(ESData, aggregate_rows(ESData, from = "cofog"))

ESData <- merge(ESData, ESData[!is.na(cofog) & level == "main_group", .(total = sum(value)), .(year, type)],
                by = c("year", "type"), sort = FALSE)
ESData$cofogParent <- substring(ESData$cofog, 1, 4)

ESData <- merge(ESData, ESData[!is.na(cofog) & level == "main_group", .(totalParent = value, year, type, cofogParent)],
                by = c("year", "type", "cofogParent"), sort = FALSE, all.x = TRUE)

RawData <- rbind(HunData, ESData)

RawData <- merge(RawData, CofogName, by = "cofog", sort = FALSE, all.x = TRUE)
RawData <- merge(RawData, HunName, by = "huncode", sort = FALSE, all.x = TRUE)

RawData$name <- ifelse(!is.na(RawData$huncode), RawData$hunMagyar, RawData$cofogMagyar)
RawData$hunMagyar <- NULL
RawData$cofogMagyar <- NULL

RawData$prop <- RawData$value / RawData$total
RawData$propParent <- RawData$value / RawData$totalParent

InflData <- data.table(eurostat::get_eurostat("prc_hicp_aind", filters = list(geo = "HU"), cache = FALSE))

                     .(year = lubridate::year(time), inflation = 1 + values / 100)]
InflData <- rbind(data.table(year = min(InflData$year) - 1, inflation = 1), InflData)
if(2026 %notin% InflData$year) InflData <- rbind(InflData, data.table(year = 2026, inflation = 1.017))

InflData <- InflData[order(year)]
InflData$inflation <- cumprod(InflData$inflation)

                        .(year = lubridate::year(time), deflator = 1 + values / 100)]
DeflatorData <- rbind(data.table(year = min(DeflatorData$year) - 1, deflator = 1), DeflatorData)
if(2026 %notin% DeflatorData$year) DeflatorData <- rbind(DeflatorData, data.table(year = 2026, deflator = 1.040))
if(2027 %notin% DeflatorData$year) DeflatorData <- rbind(DeflatorData, data.table(year = 2027, deflator = 1.034))
DeflatorData <- DeflatorData[order(year)]
DeflatorData$deflator <- cumprod(DeflatorData$deflator)

AuxData <- merge(InflData, DeflatorData, by = "year", sort = FALSE)
AuxData <- merge(
  AuxData,
  rbind(
    GDPData[freq == "A" & unit == "CP_MNAC" & na_item == "B1GQ" & geo == "HU" & !is.na(values),
            .(year = lubridate::year(time), gdp = values)],
    data.table(year = c(2026, 2027), gdp = c(92303000, 97716000))
  ), by = "year", sort = FALSE
)

AuxData$inflation <- AuxData[year == 2025]$inflation / AuxData$inflation
AuxData$deflator <- AuxData[year == 2025]$deflator / AuxData$deflator

# RawData$date <- as.Date(paste0(RawData$year, "-01-01"))
RawData$yearchr <- as.character(RawData$year)
RawData$value <- RawData$value / 1000
RawData$prop <- RawData$prop * 100
RawData$propParent <- RawData$propParent * 100
RawData <- merge(
  RawData,
  # The label of each type of data, a factor so that the charts list the types in
  # this order
  data.table(type = c("original_plan", "actual", "actual_cofog"),
             typeLabel = c("Tervezet (pénzforgalmi)", "Tényleges (pénzforgalmi)",
                           "Tényleges (eredményszemléletű)"))[
                             , typeLabel := factor(typeLabel, levels = typeLabel)])

# The sum of `codes`, with each run of at least three consecutive codes written
# as a range (e.g. GF0101–GF0106). Codes run on their final letter (F01.a,
# F01.b) or their last two digits (F09, F10; GF0101, GF0102)
sum_label <- function(codes) {
  codes <- sort(codes)
  stem <- sub("([0-9]{2}|[a-z])$", "", codes)
  suffix <- substring(codes, nchar(stem) + 1)
  pos <- match(suffix, letters)
  pos[is.na(pos)] <- as.integer(suffix[is.na(pos)])
  run <- cumsum(c(TRUE, stem[-1] != stem[-length(stem)] | !(diff(pos) %in% 1)))
  runs <- vapply(split(codes, run), \(r) {
    if (length(r) >= 3) paste0(r[1], "\u2013", r[length(r)]) else paste(r, collapse = " + ")
  }, "")
  paste(runs, collapse = " + ")
}
aggregate_of <- vapply(aggregates, sum_label, "")
# A category's code in one classification or, if it's an aggregate, the sum it's
# built from, else a dash
code_label <- \(code, other) fcoalesce(code, unname(aggregate_of[other]), "-")
# The aggregates whose code starts with `prefix` (GF: those of COFOG, F: the
# Hungarian ones), written out for the text, e.g. "GF01 = F01 + F15, ..."
written_out <- \(prefix) {
  codes <- names(aggregates)[startsWith(names(aggregates), prefix)]
  paste(codes, "=", vapply(aggregates[codes], paste, "", collapse = " + "), collapse = ", ")
}

RawData$nameLabel <- paste0(
  RawData$name, " (Magyar: ", code_label(RawData$huncode, RawData$cofog),
  ", COFOG: ", code_label(RawData$cofog, RawData$huncode), ")"
)
RawData$nameLabel <- factor(RawData$nameLabel,
                            levels = unique(RawData[order(huncode, cofog)]$nameLabel))
RawData <- merge(RawData, AuxData, by = "year", sort = FALSE)
RawData$propgdp <- RawData$value / (RawData$gdp / 1000) * 100
RawData <- RawData[order(year)]

RawData$valuedefl <- RawData$value * RawData$deflator
RawData$valueinfl <- RawData$value * RawData$inflation

# Where each row of RawData sits in the Hungarian and in the COFOG hierarchy:
# under its main group (huncodeParent / cofogParent), as "Összesen" if it's the main group
# itself. Rows present in both (e.g. Egészségügy: F05 = GF07) appear in both
CategoryPaths <- rbind(
  RawData[, .(classification = "Magyar", node = huncode, parent = huncodeParent,
              nameLabel, key = .I)],
  RawData[, .(classification = "Nemzetközi (COFOG)", node = cofog,
              parent = cofogParent, nameLabel, key = .I)]
)[!is.na(node)]
CategoryPaths[, `:=`(
  main = as.character(nameLabel[node == parent][1]),
  sub = fifelse(node == parent, "Összesen", as.character(nameLabel))
), by = .(classification, parent)]
# The dropdowns list the categories in this order
setorder(CategoryPaths, classification, parent, node)

# Radio buttons with the values `choices`, labelled by its names if it has any
# (as in shiny::radioButtons). `compact = TRUE` shows the choices as a group of
# small toggle buttons (stretched to the available width) with a small label and
# no margin below, for placing it next to other filters; `inline` is then ignored
radio_buttons <- function(id, label, choices, selected = choices[[1]], inline = FALSE,
                          compact = FALSE) {
  labels <- if (is.null(names(choices))) choices else names(choices)
  radios <- lapply(seq_along(choices), \(i) {
    input_id <- paste0(id, "_", i)
    input <- htmltools::tags$input(
      class = if (compact) "btn-check" else "form-check-input", type = "radio",
      name = id, id = input_id, value = choices[[i]],
      checked = if (choices[[i]] == selected) NA
    )
    if (compact) {
      # Bootstrap draws the label right after a .btn-check input as its button
      htmltools::tagList(input, htmltools::tags$label(
        class = "btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary", `for` = input_id, labels[[i]]
      ))
    } else {
      htmltools::div(
        class = "form-check", class = if (inline) "form-check-inline", input,
        htmltools::tags$label(class = "form-check-label", `for` = input_id, labels[[i]])
      )
    }
  })
  if (compact) radios <- htmltools::div(class = "btn-group d-flex", radios)
  
  htmltools::tags$fieldset(
    id = id, class = if (!compact) "mb-3",
    htmltools::tags$legend(
      class = "form-label", class = if (compact) "small mb-1" else "fs-6", label
    ),
    radios
  )
}

# crosstalk has no radio-button filter, so this builds one on crosstalk's JS API,
# with the buttons of radio_buttons() (which describes `inline` and `compact`)
filter_radio <- function(id, label, sharedData, group, selected = NULL, inline = FALSE,
                         compact = FALSE) {
  df <- sharedData$origData()
  values <- if (inherits(group, "formula")) {
    eval(group[[2]], df, environment(group))
  } else group
  lvls <- if (is.factor(values)) levels(droplevels(values)) else sort(unique(values))
  lvls <- as.character(lvls)
  if (is.null(selected)) selected <- lvls[1]
  keys <- as.character(sharedData$key())
  map <- setNames(lapply(lvls, \(l) keys[which(values == l)]), lvls)
  
  # Set the filter only after the widgets have rendered: echarts4r reacts to
  # filter changes, but ignores a filter that was set before it existed
  js <- sprintf(
    "HTMLWidgets.addPostRenderHandler(function() {
      var map = %s;
      var handle = new crosstalk.FilterHandle(%s);
      var inputs = document.getElementById(%s).querySelectorAll('input');
      function update() {
        inputs.forEach(function(el) { if (el.checked) handle.set(map[el.value]); });
      }
      inputs.forEach(function(el) { el.addEventListener('change', update); });
      update();
    });",
    jsonlite::toJSON(map),
    jsonlite::toJSON(sharedData$groupName(), auto_unbox = TRUE),
    jsonlite::toJSON(id, auto_unbox = TRUE)
  )
  
  htmltools::attachDependencies(
    htmltools::tagList(
      radio_buttons(id, label, lvls, selected, inline = inline, compact = compact),
      htmltools::tags$script(htmltools::HTML(js))
    ),
    crosstalk::crosstalkLibs()
  )
}

# crosstalk's filter_select can't depend on other filters, so this is a
# single-choice dropdown (without an "(All)" option) that only offers the values
# of `group` occurring in the rows that match the current choice of each parent
# filter: the filter_radio or filter_select_dependent elements in `parent_id`,
# with their grouping variables in `parent_group` (a list if there are several).
# Values are offered in their order of appearance, and a choice keeps only its
# rows within the parents' choices, so a key may occur in several rows (e.g.
# once under each classification). `compact = TRUE` makes the dropdown and its
# label smaller, without margin below, as in filter_radio
filter_select_dependent <- function(id, label, sharedData, group, parent_id,
                                    parent_group, selected = NULL, compact = FALSE) {
  df <- sharedData$origData()
  eval_group <- \(g) {
    as.character(if (inherits(g, "formula")) eval(g[[2]], df, environment(g)) else g)
  }
  if (!is.list(parent_group)) parent_group <- list(parent_group)
  values <- eval_group(group)
  keys <- as.character(sharedData$key())
  # Joined the same way as the parents' current choices in the JavaScript below
  parents <- do.call(paste, c(lapply(parent_group, eval_group), sep = "\u001f"))
  rows <- split(seq_along(values), parents)
  choices <- lapply(rows, \(i) unique(values[i]))
  map <- lapply(rows, \(i) split(keys[i], values[i]))
  
  js <- sprintf(
    "HTMLWidgets.addPostRenderHandler(function() {
      var choices = %s, map = %s, selected = %s;
      var select = document.getElementById(%s);
      var parents = %s.map(function(id) { return document.getElementById(id); });
      var handle = new crosstalk.FilterHandle(%s);

      function parentKey() {
        return parents.map(function(el) {
          return el.tagName === 'SELECT' ? el.value :
            el.querySelector('input:checked').value;
        }).join('\\u001f');
      }

      function update() {
        var offered = choices[parentKey()] || [];
        // Keep the current choice if it's still offered, else fall back to `selected`
        var value = [select.value, selected]
          .find(function(v) { return offered.includes(v); }) || offered[0];
        select.replaceChildren.apply(select, offered.map(function(v) {
          return new Option(v, v, false, v === value);
        }));
        // Also updates the filters that depend on this one
        select.dispatchEvent(new Event('change'));
      }

      select.addEventListener('change', function() {
        handle.set((map[parentKey()] || {})[select.value] || []);
      });
      parents.forEach(function(el) { el.addEventListener('change', update); });
      update();
    });",
    jsonlite::toJSON(choices),
    jsonlite::toJSON(map),
    jsonlite::toJSON(selected, auto_unbox = TRUE, null = "null"),
    jsonlite::toJSON(id, auto_unbox = TRUE),
    jsonlite::toJSON(parent_id),
    jsonlite::toJSON(sharedData$groupName(), auto_unbox = TRUE)
  )
  
  htmltools::attachDependencies(
    htmltools::tagList(
      htmltools::div(
        class = if (!compact) "mb-3",
        htmltools::tags$label(
          class = "form-label", class = if (compact) "small mb-1", `for` = id, label
        ),
        htmltools::tags$select(
          id = id, class = "form-select", class = if (compact) "form-select-sm"
        )
      ),
      htmltools::tags$script(htmltools::HTML(js))
    ),
    crosstalk::crosstalkLibs()
  )
}

# filter_radio with choices that depend on other filters, the way the choices of
# filter_select_dependent do (which describes `parent_id`, `parent_group` and how
# the choice is kept when they change): it only offers the values of `group`
# occurring in the rows that match the parents' current choices, in the order
# filter_radio would offer them, and shows its buttons even if it offers a single
# value. `inline` and `compact` are as in radio_buttons()
filter_radio_dependent <- function(id, label, sharedData, group, parent_id,
                                   parent_group, selected = NULL, inline = FALSE,
                                   compact = FALSE) {
  df <- sharedData$origData()
  eval_group <- \(g) if (inherits(g, "formula")) eval(g[[2]], df, environment(g)) else g
  if (!is.list(parent_group)) parent_group <- list(parent_group)
  values <- eval_group(group)
  lvls <- as.character(
    if (is.factor(values)) levels(droplevels(values)) else sort(unique(values))
  )
  values <- as.character(values)
  keys <- as.character(sharedData$key())
  # Joined the same way as the parents' current choices in the JavaScript below
  parents <- do.call(paste, c(lapply(parent_group, \(g) as.character(eval_group(g))),
                              sep = "\u001f"))
  rows <- split(seq_along(values), parents)
  fieldsets <- lapply(rows, \(i) {
    offered <- intersect(lvls, values[i])
    radio_buttons(id, label, offered,
                  selected = if (isTRUE(selected %in% offered)) selected else offered[[1]],
                  inline = inline, compact = compact)
  })
  map <- lapply(rows, \(i) split(keys[i], values[i]))
  
  js <- sprintf(
    "HTMLWidgets.addPostRenderHandler(function() {
      var contents = %s, map = %s, selected = %s;
      var fieldset = document.getElementById(%s);
      var parents = %s.map(function(id) { return document.getElementById(id); });
      var handle = new crosstalk.FilterHandle(%s);

      function parentKey() {
        return parents.map(function(el) {
          return el.tagName === 'SELECT' ? el.value :
            el.querySelector('input:checked').value;
        }).join('\\u001f');
      }

      function value() {
        var checked = fieldset.querySelector('input:checked');
        return checked && checked.value;
      }

      function update() {
        var current = value();
        fieldset.innerHTML = contents[parentKey()] || '';
        var inputs = Array.from(fieldset.querySelectorAll('input'));
        var offered = inputs.map(function(el) { return el.value; });
        // Keep the current choice if it's still offered, else fall back to `selected`
        var choice = [current, selected]
          .find(function(v) { return offered.includes(v); }) || offered[0];
        inputs.forEach(function(el) { el.checked = el.value === choice; });
        // Also updates the filters that depend on this one
        fieldset.dispatchEvent(new Event('change'));
      }

      fieldset.addEventListener('change', function() {
        handle.set((map[parentKey()] || {})[value()] || []);
      });
      parents.forEach(function(el) { el.addEventListener('change', update); });
      update();
    });",
    # What goes inside the fieldset (the legend and the buttons) for each choice of
    # the parents
    jsonlite::toJSON(lapply(fieldsets, \(f) as.character(htmltools::tagList(f$children))),
                     auto_unbox = TRUE),
    jsonlite::toJSON(map),
    jsonlite::toJSON(selected, auto_unbox = TRUE, null = "null"),
    jsonlite::toJSON(id, auto_unbox = TRUE),
    jsonlite::toJSON(parent_id),
    jsonlite::toJSON(sharedData$groupName(), auto_unbox = TRUE)
  )
  
  htmltools::attachDependencies(
    htmltools::tagList(
      # The buttons for the parents' first combination of values, until the
      # JavaScript reads their current choices
      fieldsets[[1]],
      htmltools::tags$script(htmltools::HTML(js))
    ),
    crosstalk::crosstalkLibs()
  )
}

# Puts `chart` in a box with a download button (a dropdown with the id `id`) over
# its top right corner, whose menu saves the chart as a PNG, a JPG or an SVG, or
# the data it plots, as shown, in an Excel or a CSV file: a column of the x values,
# then the plotted column of each series left by the filters and the legend, headed
# by its name and `unit`. The images show the whole legend, even where the chart
# scrolls it, and are taller for it. The files are named after the title of the
# chart and, if the plotted column is chosen with the radio buttons `choice_id`, the
# chosen one. With `download_axis_name = TRUE`, both data files start with a line of
# the name of the y axis, as shown (in one line). The Excel file is put together here
# (as a zip of a few XML files), so that the page needs no library for it. As the
# result is no longer a widget, this comes after everything else done to the chart
add_download_menu <- function(chart, unit, id, choice_id = NULL,
                              download_axis_name = FALSE) {
  chart <- htmlwidgets::onRender(chart, r"-(
                        function(el, x, data) {
                        var chart = echarts.getInstanceByDom(el);
                        
                        // The rows of the table, the header first, with the x values in their order
                        // on the axis, and an empty cell (undefined) where a series has no value
                        function table() {
                        var model = chart.getModel(), axis = model.getComponent('xAxis');
                        var header = [axis.get('name')], rows = {}, columnOf = {};
                        // Skips the series hidden with the legend; those filtered out have no data.
                        // Series of the same name (in stack mode, the negative and the positive
                        // parts of a category) share a column, with their values added up
                        model.eachSeries(function(series) {
                        var points = series.getData(), y = points.mapDimension('y');
                        var j = columnOf[series.name] || header.length;
                        for (var i = 0; i < points.count(); i++) {
                        var name = points.getName(i), value = points.get(y, i);
                        if (isNaN(value)) continue;
                        // A year as a number, so that Excel takes it for one
                        rows[name] = rows[name] || [isNaN(name) ? name : Number(name)];
                        rows[name][j] = (rows[name][j] || 0) + value;
                        if (j === header.length) {
                        columnOf[series.name] = j;
                        header.push(series.name + ' [' + data.unit + ']');
                        }
                        }
                        });
                        var order = axis.get('data');
                        return [header].concat(Object.keys(rows)
                        .sort(function(a, b) { return order.indexOf(a) - order.indexOf(b); })
                        .map(function(name) {
                        return header.map(function(_, j) { return rows[name][j]; });
                        }));
                        }
                        
                        // The name of the y axis, in one line, if the files are to start with it
                        // (read at the click, as it changes with the plotted column)
                        function caption() {
                        if (data.downloadAxisName) {
                        return chart.getModel().getComponent('yAxis').get('name').replace(/\n/g, ' ');
                        }
                        }
                        
                        // With 15 significant digits, as R writes numbers, which drops the noise of
                        // floating-point arithmetic (as in 0.30000000000000004)
                        function number(value) {
                        return String(Number(value.toPrecision(15)));
                        }
                        
                        // Semicolons between the columns and decimal commas, as Excel expects them
                        // with Hungarian regional settings. `caption`, if any, is a line before the
                        // rows
                        function csv(rows, caption) {
                        var text = (caption ? [[caption]] : []).concat(rows).map(function(row) {
                        return row.map(function(cell) {
                        if (cell === undefined) return '';
                        if (typeof cell === 'number') return number(cell).replace('.', ',');
                        return /[";\r\n]/.test(cell) ? '"' + cell.replace(/"/g, '""') + '"' : cell;
                        }).join(';');
                        }).join('\r\n');
                        // The byte order mark tells Excel that the file is in UTF-8
                        return new Blob(['\ufeff' + text + '\r\n'], { type: 'text/csv;charset=utf-8' });
                        }
                        
                        // `caption`, if any, is a row before the rows, in one cell, which spills over
                        // the empty ones next to it, so the columns aren't widened for it
                        function xlsx(rows, caption) {
                        // The name of the j-th column (from 0): A to Z, then AA, AB...
                        function column(j) {
                        return (j >= 26 ? column(Math.floor(j / 26) - 1) : '') +
                        String.fromCharCode(65 + j % 26);
                        }
                        var sheetData = (caption ? [[caption]] : []).concat(rows).map(function(row, i) {
                        return '<row r="' + (i + 1) + '">' + row.map(function(cell, j) {
                        var ref = ' r="' + column(j) + (i + 1) + '"';
                        if (cell === undefined) return '';
                        if (typeof cell === 'number') return '<c' + ref + '><v>' + number(cell) + '</v></c>';
                        cell = cell.replace(/&/g, '&amp;').replace(/</g, '&lt;').replace(/>/g, '&gt;');
                        return '<c' + ref + ' t="inlineStr"><is><t>' + cell + '</t></is></c>';
                        }).join('') + '</row>';
                        }).join('');
                        // Each column wide enough for its header, within limits
                        var cols = rows[0].map(function(name, j) {
                        return '<col min="' + (j + 1) + '" max="' + (j + 1) + '" width="' +
                        Math.min(Math.max(name.length + 2, 10), 50) + '" customWidth="1"/>';
                        }).join('');
                        var ns = 'http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/';
                        var type = 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-';
                        return zip({
                        '[Content_Types].xml':
                        '<Types xmlns="' + ns + 'package/2006/content-types">' +
                        '<Default Extension="rels" ContentType="' + type + 'package.relationships+xml"/>' +
                        '<Default Extension="xml" ContentType="application/xml"/>' +
                        '<Override PartName="/xl/workbook.xml" ContentType="' + type +
                        'officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet.main+xml"/>' +
                        '<Override PartName="/xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml" ContentType="' + type +
                        'officedocument.spreadsheetml.worksheet+xml"/></Types>',
                        '_rels/.rels':
                        '<Relationships xmlns="' + ns + 'package/2006/relationships">' +
                        '<Relationship Id="rId1" Target="xl/workbook.xml" Type="' + ns +
                        'officeDocument/2006/relationships/officeDocument"/></Relationships>',
                        'xl/workbook.xml':
                        '<workbook xmlns="' + ns + 'spreadsheetml/2006/main" xmlns:r="' + ns +
                        'officeDocument/2006/relationships"><sheets>' +
                        '<sheet name="Adatok" sheetId="1" r:id="rId1"/></sheets></workbook>',
                        'xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels':
                        '<Relationships xmlns="' + ns + 'package/2006/relationships">' +
                        '<Relationship Id="rId1" Target="worksheets/sheet1.xml" Type="' + ns +
                        'officeDocument/2006/relationships/worksheet"/></Relationships>',
                        'xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml':
                        '<worksheet xmlns="' + ns + 'spreadsheetml/2006/main"><cols>' + cols +
                        '</cols><sheetData>' + sheetData + '</sheetData></worksheet>'
                        }, type + 'officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet');
                        }
                        
                        // A zip archive of the XML documents `files` (their contents by name), as a
                        // Blob of the MIME type `type`, with the files stored uncompressed
                        function zip(files, type) {
                        var crcTable = Array.from({ length: 256 }, function(_, c) {
                        for (var k = 0; k < 8; k++) c = c & 1 ? 0xEDB88320 ^ (c >>> 1) : c >>> 1;
                        return c;
                        });
                        // The integers `values`, little-endian, each of the size in bytes in `sizes`
                        function bytes(values, sizes) {
                        var view = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(sizes.reduce(function(a, b) { return a + b; })));
                        values.reduce(function(at, value, i) {
                        view[sizes[i] === 2 ? 'setUint16' : 'setUint32'](at, value, true);
                        return at + sizes[i];
                        }, 0);
                        return new Uint8Array(view.buffer);
                        }
                        var encoder = new TextEncoder(), local = [], central = [], offset = 0;
                        Object.keys(files).forEach(function(name) {
                        var path = encoder.encode(name);
                        var content = encoder.encode(
                        '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>\n' + files[name]
                        );
                        var crc = ~content.reduce(function(c, byte) {
                        return crcTable[(c ^ byte) & 255] ^ (c >>> 8);
                        }, -1) >>> 0;
                        // The fields that both headers of the file have, from the version needed
                        // to extract it (2.0): no flags, no compression, modified on 1980-01-01 at
                        // 0:00, the CRC-32 and the sizes, the length of the name and of the extra
                        // field
                        var common = [20, 0, 0, 0, 33, crc, content.length, content.length, path.length, 0];
                        var sizes = [2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 4, 4, 4, 2, 2];
                        local.push(bytes([0x04034b50].concat(common), [4].concat(sizes)), path, content);
                        // Also with the version that made it and where its local header is
                        central.push(bytes([0x02014b50, 20].concat(common, [0, 0, 0, 0, offset]),
                        [4, 2].concat(sizes, [2, 2, 2, 4, 4])), path);
                        offset += 30 + path.length + content.length;
                        });
                        var size = central.reduce(function(total, part) { return total + part.length; }, 0);
                        var count = Object.keys(files).length;
                        var end = bytes([0x06054b50, 0, 0, count, count, size, offset, 0],
                        [4, 2, 2, 2, 2, 4, 4, 2]);
                        return new Blob(local.concat(central, [end]), { type: type });
                        }
                        
                        // The title of the chart and, if the plotted column is chosen with radio
                        // buttons, the chosen one (the first one if the buttons are hidden), without
                        // the characters that Windows doesn't allow in file names
                        function fileName() {
                        var parts = [];
                        chart.getModel().eachComponent('title', function(title) {
                        parts.push(title.get('text'));
                        });
                        var choice = data.choiceId && document.getElementById(data.choiceId);
                        if (choice) {
                        var input = choice.parentElement.hidden ? choice.querySelector('input') :
                        choice.querySelector('input:checked');
                        parts.push(choice.querySelector('label[for="' + input.id + '"]').textContent);
                        }
                        return (parts.filter(Boolean).join(', ') || 'adatok')
                        .replace(/\n/g, ' ').replace(/: /g, ' - ').replace(/[\\/:*?"<>|]/g, '-');
                        }
                        
                        // The height of the legend of the chart `c` (of its items)
                        function legendHeight(c) {
                        var model = c.getModel().getComponent('legend');
                        var view = model && c.getViewOfComponentModel(model);
                        return view ? view.getContentGroup().getBoundingRect().height : 0;
                        }
                        
                        // A copy of the chart as shown, for an image, drawn with ECharts' `renderer`
                        // ('canvas' or 'svg'), without animation, on the background of the chart or
                        // else white, as ECharts' own saveAsImage button would. Its legend is shown
                        // whole, as an image can't scroll it, and the copy is taller than the chart by
                        // the room that takes
                        function copyOf(renderer) {
                        var width = chart.getWidth(), height = chart.getHeight();
                        // The canvas copy is drawn at the pixel ratio of the images (see bitmap()), not
                        // the screen's: ECharts would scale a copy with a higher one (as on phones) down
                        // to theirs, blurring them slightly
                        var copy = renderer === 'svg' ?
                        echarts.init(null, null, { renderer: 'svg', ssr: true, width: width, height: height }) :
                        echarts.init(document.createElement('div'), null,
                        { width: width, height: height, devicePixelRatio: 2 });
                        var option = chart.getOption();
                        option.animation = false;
                        option.backgroundColor = chart.getModel().get('backgroundColor') || '#fff';
                        (option.legend || []).forEach(function(legend) { legend.type = 'plain'; });
                        copy.setOption(option);
                        // If a name is too long for a line of the legend (as on phones), the legend
                        // becomes a column of the names broken into lines as wide as the room beside
                        // the icon and the 5px gap after it. (Not rows, as ECharts would let the names
                        // of more lines overlap the row above. Laid out in a chart tall enough not to
                        // wrap the column into more)
                        var legendModel = copy.getModel().getComponent('legend');
                        if (legendModel) {
                        // The padding of the legend is given as in CSS
                        var padding = [].concat(legendModel.get('padding'));
                        var right = padding.length > 1 ? padding[1] : padding[0];
                        var room = width - right - (padding.length > 3 ? padding[3] : right);
                        var items = copy.getViewOfComponentModel(legendModel).getContentGroup();
                        if (items.getBoundingRect().width > room) {
                        copy.resize({ width: width, height: 10 * height });
                        copy.setOption({ legend: {
                        orient: 'vertical',
                        textStyle: {
                        width: room - legendModel.get('itemWidth') - 5, overflow: 'break',
                        // ECharts would set the lines as close as the size of the font, so that the
                        // accents of a line touch the one above
                        lineHeight: Math.round(1.4 * (legendModel.get(['textStyle', 'fontSize']) || 12))
                        }
                        } });
                        }
                        }
                        var extra = Math.round(legendHeight(copy) - legendHeight(chart));
                        copy.setOption({ grid: { bottom: option.grid[0].bottom + extra } });
                        copy.resize({ width: width, height: height + extra });
                        return copy;
                        }
                        
                        // The chart as shown, as the data URL of a PNG or a JPG (`type` 'png' or
                        // 'jpeg'), at twice the resolution
                        function bitmap(type) {
                        var copy = copyOf('canvas');
                        var url = copy.getDataURL({ type: type, pixelRatio: 2 });
                        copy.dispose();
                        return url;
                        }
                        
                        // The chart as shown, in an SVG file
                        function svg() {
                        var copy = copyOf('svg');
                        var text = copy.renderToSVGString();
                        copy.dispose();
                        return new Blob([text], { type: 'image/svg+xml' });
                        }
                        
                        // `file` is a Blob or, for a PNG or a JPG, a data URL
                        function save(file, extension) {
                        var link = document.createElement('a');
                        link.href = file instanceof Blob ? URL.createObjectURL(file) : file;
                        link.download = fileName() + '.' + extension;
                        document.body.appendChild(link);
                        link.click();
                        link.remove();
                        // Once the download has surely started
                        if (file instanceof Blob) {
                        setTimeout(function() { URL.revokeObjectURL(link.href); }, 60000);
                        }
                        }
                        
                        // Each item of the menu saves in the format it names
                        var menu = document.getElementById(data.menuId);
                        menu.addEventListener('click', function(event) {
                        var item = event.target.closest('[data-format]');
                        if (!item) return;
                        var format = item.dataset.format;
                        if (format === 'png' || format === 'jpg') {
                        save(bitmap(format === 'jpg' ? 'jpeg' : 'png'), format);
                        } else if (format === 'svg') {
                        save(svg(), 'svg');
                        } else {
                        save((format === 'csv' ? csv : xlsx)(table(), caption()), format);
                        }
                        // The menu closes, so keyboard users are taken back to the button
                        menu.querySelector('[data-bs-toggle]').focus();
                        });
                        }
  )-", data = list(unit = unit, menuId = id, choiceId = choice_id,
                   downloadAxisName = download_axis_name))
  
  item <- \(format, label) htmltools::tags$li(htmltools::tags$button(
    # Taller than Bootstrap's default, to be easier to tap
    type = "button", class = "dropdown-item py-2", `data-format` = format, label
  ))
  htmltools::div(
    class = "position-relative",
    chart,
    # After the chart, so that it's drawn over it
    htmltools::div(
      id = id, class = "dropdown position-absolute", style = "top: 0; right: 10px",
      htmltools::tags$button(
        type = "button", class = "btn btn-outline-secondary p-0",
        class = "d-flex align-items-center justify-content-center",
        # Of a set size, as the title of the chart is wrapped to clear it, possibly
        # before the font of the icon has loaded
        style = "width: 2.5rem; height: 2.5rem",
        `data-bs-toggle` = "dropdown", `aria-expanded` = "false",
        `aria-label` = "Letöltés", title = "Letöltés",
        htmltools::tags$i(class = "bi bi-download", `aria-hidden` = "true")
      ),
      htmltools::tags$ul(
        class = "dropdown-menu dropdown-menu-end",
        item("png", "Mentés képként (PNG)"),
        item("jpg", "Mentés képként (JPG)"),
        item("svg", "Mentés képként (SVG)"),
        htmltools::tags$li(htmltools::tags$hr(class = "dropdown-divider")),
        item("xlsx", "Adatok letöltése (XLSX)"),
        item("csv", "Adatok letöltése (CSV)")
      )
    )
  )
}

# The filters and the chart of the column `var` of RawData in "Eredmények", with
# `axis_name` on the y axis and `unit` after the values in the tooltip. The chart
# has no title if `title` is NULL, else `title` followed by the name of the chosen
# main group and, unless it's "Összesen", of the subgroup. If `var` has several
# columns, the chart plots the one chosen with radio buttons labelled `var_label`,
# which offer them by their names (the first one by default), and `axis_name` may
# give a different name for each. With `stack = TRUE`, the chart instead shows what
# the chosen main group is made of, as the stacked areas of its subgroups (or, for
# "Összesen", of the main groups), for the type of data chosen with radio buttons
# in place of the subgroup dropdown, which only offer the types of data that come
# in the chosen classification. The title then names the main group (unless it's
# "Összesen") and the type, and the tooltip only shows the hovered area. The radio
# buttons for `var` only appear when a main group is chosen, as the columns after
# the first may be relative to it (like propParent): for "Összesen", the chart
# plots the first column. With `download_axis_name = TRUE`, the downloadable CSV
# and Excel files start with a line of the name of the y axis, which tells what the
# values are (e.g. which column is plotted). Each call has its own crosstalk group
# and element ids (made from `id`), so its controls only affect its own chart
category_chart <- function(var, axis_name, unit, title = NULL, var_label = NULL,
                           stack = FALSE, download_axis_name = FALSE,
                           id = paste0(var[[1]], if (stack) "_stack")) {
  axis_name <- rep_len(axis_name, length(var))
  group <- paste0("category_", id)
  filter_ids <- paste0(id, c("_classification_filter", "_main_group_filter",
                             "_subgroup_filter", "_type_filter"))
  var_id <- paste0(id, "_var_choice")
  download_id <- paste0(id, "_download")
  
  # The filters pick the plotted rows by their keys, as the two share a crosstalk
  # group. The chart only gets the columns it plots, since echarts4r embeds every
  # column in the page
  if (stack) {
    # A row of RawData in both classifications (e.g. Egészségügy) is a part of a
    # different whole in each, so here a key is a row of CategoryPaths, i.e. a row
    # of RawData in one classification. The main group dropdown picks the whole: a
    # main group, made up of its subgroups, or "Összesen", made up of the main
    # groups. Each type of data only appears in the classification it comes in
    # (the budget's cash-based data in the Hungarian one, Eurostat's accrual-based
    # data in COFOG), as only there do the parts add up to the whole: the
    # categories mapped from the other classification leave gaps
    native <- c(original_plan = "Magyar", actual = "Magyar",
                actual_cofog = "Nemzetközi (COFOG)")
    paths <- CategoryPaths[classification == native[RawData$type[key]], .(
      classification, main = fifelse(sub == "Összesen", "Összesen", main),
      typeLabel = RawData$typeLabel[key], nameLabel, row = key, key = .I
    )]
    # A series for each part in each classification, stacked in the order of the
    # codes. Named by its number, as echarts4r writes the name into every row
    paths[, series := paste(classification, nameLabel)]
    paths[, series := factor(series, levels = unique(series),
                             labels = seq_along(unique(series)))]
    shared_paths <- crosstalk::SharedData$new(
      # "Összesen" first in the dropdown
      paths[order(main != "Összesen")], key = ~key, group = group
    )
    # In the order of the years, as echarts4r puts them on the x axis in the order
    # they first appear in
    chart_data <- RawData[paths$row, c("yearchr", var), with = FALSE][
      , `:=`(series = paths$series, key = paths$key)][order(yearchr)]
    # Each column split into its negative part, in a column of its name with
    # "_neg" appended, and its positive part, in the column itself, as the two are
    # stacked separately (see the series below). The negative part is missing
    # except around the years when it's below 0 (with 0 in the years just before
    # and after, so that its area tapers off), as a series of zeros would still
    # draw its line along 0
    neg_var <- paste0(var, "_neg")
    chart_data[, (neg_var) := lapply(.SD, \(x) {
      below <- !is.na(x) & x < 0
      fcase(below, x,
            shift(below, fill = FALSE) | shift(below, type = "lead", fill = FALSE), 0)
    }), by = series, .SDcols = var]
    chart_data[, (var) := lapply(.SD, pmax, 0), .SDcols = var]
    shared_data <- crosstalk::SharedData$new(
      chart_data[, !"key"] |> dplyr::group_by(series),
      key = as.character(chart_data$key), group = group
    )
  } else {
    # A key is the row number in RawData (the default key of shared_data)
    shared_paths <- crosstalk::SharedData$new(CategoryPaths, key = ~key, group = group)
    shared_data <- crosstalk::SharedData$new(
      RawData[, c("typeLabel", "yearchr", var), with = FALSE] |>
        dplyr::group_by(typeLabel),
      group = group
    )
  }
  
  # The filters share a row on wide screens, but the dropdowns are at least 20rem
  # wide, so on narrower screens they wrap onto rows of their own. (A Bootstrap
  # .row would overflow, as Quarto sets overflow-x: auto on the cell output)
  filters <- htmltools::div(
    class = "d-flex flex-wrap align-items-end row-gap-2 mb-3",
    # Not Bootstrap's column-gap-3: Quarto mistakes any class starting with
    # "column-" for a layout class like column-page, and turns the section into a
    # grid that confines its content to the narrower body column
    style = "column-gap: 1rem",
    htmltools::div(
      # Full width on phones, where it's alone in its row
      class = "flex-grow-1 flex-md-grow-0",
      filter_radio(
        id = filter_ids[1],
        label = "Osztályozás:",
        sharedData = shared_paths,
        group = ~classification,
        selected = "Magyar",
        compact = TRUE
      )
    ),
    if (stack) htmltools::div(
      class = "flex-grow-1 flex-md-grow-0",
      # Before the main group dropdown, so that when the classification changes,
      # this is updated first, and the dropdown never looks for the main groups of
      # a type that the new classification doesn't have (which would lose its
      # choice)
      filter_radio_dependent(
        id = filter_ids[4],
        label = "Adat:",
        sharedData = shared_paths,
        group = ~typeLabel,
        parent_id = filter_ids[1],
        parent_group = ~classification,
        selected = "Tervezet (pénzforgalmi)",
        compact = TRUE
      )
    ),
    htmltools::div(
      style = "flex: 1 1 20rem",
      filter_select_dependent(
        id = filter_ids[2],
        label = "Főcsoport:",
        sharedData = shared_paths,
        group = ~main,
        # In stack mode, only the main groups with subgroups of the chosen type
        parent_id = filter_ids[if (stack) c(1, 4) else 1],
        parent_group = if (stack) list(~classification, ~typeLabel) else ~classification,
        selected = if (stack) "Összesen" else "Egészségügy (Magyar: F05, COFOG: GF07)",
        compact = TRUE
      )
    ),
    if (!stack) htmltools::div(
      style = "flex: 1 1 20rem",
      filter_select_dependent(
        id = filter_ids[3],
        label = "Csoport:",
        sharedData = shared_paths,
        group = ~sub,
        parent_id = filter_ids[1:2],
        parent_group = list(~classification, ~main),
        selected = "Összesen",
        compact = TRUE
      )
    ),
    if (length(var) > 1) htmltools::div(
      class = "flex-grow-1 flex-md-grow-0",
      # In stack mode, until a main group is chosen (see below)
      hidden = if (stack) NA,
      radio_buttons(id = var_id, label = var_label, choices = var, compact = TRUE)
    )
  )
  
  chart <- shared_data |>
    # Hovering the legend highlights nothing if the chart had more than
    # hoverLayerThreshold (by default 3000) elements when last redrawn, as it has
    # here: the points of all categories, drawn before filtering, are still
    # fading out
    e_chart(yearchr, hoverLayerThreshold = 1e6, elementId = paste0(id, "_chart"))
  chart <- if (stack) {
    # Each category as two series, of its negative and of its positive parts, each
    # stacked only on the series of the same sign, so the negative parts go below
    # 0 and the positive ones above. (ECharts' default would stack a value on the
    # values of its sign, which draws a category that is negative in a year as an
    # area diving from its place in the stack to below 0 and back, and stacks a 0
    # on the negative values if no category before it is positive in that year.)
    # The series of the negative parts come first, with a symbol only where the
    # part is below 0, not at the zeros around it. triggerLineEvent: hovering an
    # area, not only its points, tells which one it is, for the tooltip
    chart |>
      e_area_(neg_var[[1]], stack = "total", stackStrategy = "negative",
              emphasis = list(focus = "series"), triggerLineEvent = TRUE,
              symbolSize = htmlwidgets::JS("
                function(value, params) {
                  return value[params.dimensionNames[params.encode.y[0]]] < 0 ? 4 : 0;
                }
              ")) |>
      e_area_(var[[1]], stack = "total", stackStrategy = "positive",
              emphasis = list(focus = "series"), triggerLineEvent = TRUE)
  } else {
    e_line_(chart, var[[1]], emphasis = list(focus = "series"))
  }
  # After the values, in the tooltip and in the description for screen readers: a
  # space before the unit, but not before a percent sign
  unit_suffix <- if (unit == "%") unit else paste0(" ", unit)
  chart <- chart |>
    e_tooltip(trigger = "axis",
              formatter = htmlwidgets::JS(sprintf("
                function(params) {
                  return params[0].name + '<br>' +
                    params.map(function(p) {
                      // With crosstalk, p.value is the whole data row as an object,
                      // not [x, y], so this reads the plotted column from it
                      var column = p.dimensionNames[p.encode.y[0]];
                      // One decimal, or two significant digits if that's more
                      // precise (below 1), so that small values aren't rounded to 0
                      var value = Number(p.value[column]).toLocaleString('hu-HU', {
                        maximumFractionDigits: 1, maximumSignificantDigits: 2,
                        roundingPriority: 'morePrecision'
                      });

                      return p.marker + ' ' + p.seriesName +
                        ': <b>' + value + '%s</b>';
                    }).join('<br>');
                }", unit_suffix))) |>
    e_title(subtext = "Ferenci Tamás (medstat.hu)", bottom = 0, right = 10,
            sublink = "https://www.medstat.hu/", subtarget = "blank") |>
    e_x_axis(name = "Év") |>
    e_y_axis(name = axis_name[[1]],
             axisLabel = list(
               # toLocaleString keeps only 3 decimals by default, too few for the
               # ticks of the smallest categories
               formatter = htmlwidgets::JS("
                function(value) {
                  return value.toLocaleString('hu-HU', { maximumFractionDigits: 20 });
                }
              ")
             ))
  
  # For screen readers, the chart is an image, described by its title, its axes and
  # the values shown, formatted as in the tooltip. (ECharts' own description, with
  # e_aria(), would be in English and list every column of the data, for every
  # series, even the ones filtered out)
  chart <- chart |>
    htmlwidgets::onRender("
      function(el, x, data) {
        var chart = echarts.getInstanceByDom(el);
        var format = new Intl.NumberFormat('hu-HU', {
          maximumFractionDigits: 1, maximumSignificantDigits: 2,
          roundingPriority: 'morePrecision'
        });
        el.setAttribute('role', 'img');

        // After every redraw, so whenever the filters, the plotted column, the
        // title or the legend change
        chart.on('finished', function() {
          var model = chart.getModel(), parts = [];
          model.eachComponent('title', function(title) { parts.push(title.get('text')); });
          parts.push(data.type,
                     'Vízszintes tengely: ' + model.getComponent('xAxis').get('name'),
                     'Függőleges tengely: ' + model.getComponent('yAxis').get('name'));
          // Skips the series hidden with the legend; those filtered out have no data.
          // Series of the same name (in stack mode, the negative and the positive
          // parts of a category) are added up
          var sums = new Map();
          model.eachSeries(function(series) {
            var points = series.getData(), y = points.mapDimension('y');
            var values = sums.get(series.name) || new Map();
            for (var i = 0; i < points.count(); i++) {
              var x = points.getName(i), value = points.get(y, i);
              if (!isNaN(value)) values.set(x, (values.get(x) || 0) + value);
            }
            if (values.size) sums.set(series.name, values);
          });
          sums.forEach(function(values, name) {
            parts.push(name + ': ' + Array.from(values, function(entry) {
              return entry[0] + ': ' + format.format(entry[1]) + data.unit;
            }).join('; '));
          });
          var label = parts.filter(Boolean).join('. ').replace(/\\n/g, ' ') + '.';
          // The chart is also redrawn on hover
          if (label !== el.getAttribute('aria-label')) el.setAttribute('aria-label', label);
        });
      }
    ", data = list(type = if (stack) "Halmozott területdiagram" else "Vonaldiagram",
                   unit = unit_suffix))
  
  if (length(var) > 1) {
    # Plots the chosen column, with its axis name. Also run at the start, in case
    # the browser restored an earlier choice when reloading the page. In stack
    # mode, the buttons are hidden, and the first column plotted, while the main
    # group dropdown is at "Összesen" (or still empty, before it's filled)
    chart <- chart |>
      htmlwidgets::onRender("
        function(el, x, data) {
          var chart = echarts.getInstanceByDom(el);
          var choice = document.getElementById(data.id);
          var main = data.mainId && document.getElementById(data.mainId);

          function update() {
            var whole = !!main && (!main.value || main.value === 'Összesen');
            // The div around the buttons, so that they leave no gap in the row
            choice.parentElement.hidden = whole;
            var column = whole ? choice.querySelector('input').value :
              choice.querySelector('input:checked').value;
            chart.setOption({
              series: chart.getOption().series.map(function(s) {
                // In stack mode, the series of negative parts plot the column
                // with _neg appended
                var negative = /_neg$/.test([].concat(s.encode.y)[0]);
                return { encode: { y: negative ? column + '_neg' : column } };
              }),
              yAxis: { name: data.axisNames[column] }
            });
          }

          choice.addEventListener('change', update);
          if (main) main.addEventListener('change', update);
          update();
        }
      ", data = c(list(id = var_id, axisNames = as.list(setNames(axis_name, var))),
                  if (stack) list(mainId = filter_ids[2])))
  }
  
  if (stack) {
    # echarts4r names each series after its group, but it should show the label
    # of its category (which has a series in each classification it's in)
    ids <- vapply(chart$x$opts$series, \(s) s$name, "")
    labels <- as.character(paths$nameLabel[match(ids, paths$series)])
    chart$x$opts$series <- Map(\(s, label) modifyList(s, list(name = label)),
                               chart$x$opts$series, labels)
    chart$x$opts$legend$data <- as.list(unique(labels))
    
    if (unit == "%") {
      # The positive parts of a whole stack up to 100%, but rounding errors can put
      # the top a hair above it, and negative parts too small to see push it up as
      # much as they go below 0. ECharts would then run the axis to 120, or down to
      # -20, so an overshoot of less than 0.5% of the axis is cut off, above 100 and
      # below 0. (When the top stays at or below 100, so does ECharts' own maximum)
      chart <- e_y_axis(
        chart,
        max = htmlwidgets::JS("
          function(value) {
            var range = value.max - Math.min(value.min, 0);
            return value.max > 100 && value.max - 100 < 0.005 * range ? 100 : null;
          }
        "),
        min = htmlwidgets::JS("
          function(value) {
            return value.min < 0 && -value.min < 0.005 * (value.max - value.min) ? 0 : null;
          }
        ")
      )
    }
    
    chart <- chart |>
      e_legend(type = "scroll") |>
      # ECharts' default palette has 9 colours, so this adds 7 for the 16 Hungarian
      # main groups, each picked (among colours of moderate lightness and chroma)
      # to differ as much as possible from all the colours before it, by CIEDE2000
      e_color(c("#5070dd", "#b6d634", "#505372", "#ff994d", "#0ca8df", "#ffd10a",
                "#fb628b", "#785db0", "#3fbe95", "#666018", "#a04024", "#c3b0e4",
                "#ab2965", "#167a4e", "#ae9d69", "#027588")) |>
      htmlwidgets::onRender("
        function(el, x, data) {
          var chart = echarts.getInstanceByDom(el);
          var option = chart.getOption();
          var names = option.series.map(function(s) { return s.name; });
          var palette = option.color, years = option.xAxis[0].data;

          // The chart has a series for every part of every whole, so when the
          // filters change, this shows only the series left in the legend,
          // coloured as if they were the only ones, and only the years from their
          // first to their last
          new crosstalk.FilterHandle(data.group).on('change', function(e) {
            var keys = e.value && new Set(e.value.map(String));
            var shown = {}, hasYear = {};
            option.dataset[0].source.forEach(function(row) {
              if (keys && !keys.has(String(row.XkeyX))) return;
              shown[row.series] = true;
              hasYear[row.yearchr] = true;
            });
            // Each name once, as a category has a series for its negative and one
            // for its positive parts
            var legend = [];
            names.forEach(function(name, i) {
              if (shown[data.series[i]] && legend.indexOf(name) < 0) legend.push(name);
            });
            var covered = years.filter(function(year) { return hasYear[year]; });
            var color = {};
            legend.forEach(function(name, i) {
              color[name] = palette[i % palette.length];
            });
            chart.setOption({
              legend: { data: legend },
              xAxis: {
                data: years.slice(years.indexOf(covered[0]),
                                  years.indexOf(covered[covered.length - 1]) + 1)
              },
              // Also the series of the same category in the other
              // classification, as the legend takes the colour of the first
              // series of a name
              series: names.map(function(name) {
                return color[name] ? { color: color[name] } : {};
              })
            });
          });

          // The formatter of e_tooltip() only gets the hovered category: its
          // negative part in a year when it's negative, else its positive part
          var format = option.tooltip[0].formatter, hovered = null;
          function column(p) { return p.dimensionNames[p.encode.y[0]]; }
          chart.setOption({
            tooltip: {
              formatter: function(params) {
                params = params.filter(function(p) { return p.seriesName === hovered; });
                var shown = params.filter(function(p) { return p.value[column(p)] < 0; });
                if (!shown.length) {
                  shown = params.filter(function(p) { return !/_neg$/.test(column(p)); });
                }
                return shown.length ? format(shown) : '';
              }
            }
          });

          chart.on('mouseover', 'series', function(p) {
            hovered = p.seriesName;
            // ECharts only emphasizes the hovered series, but a category has a
            // series for its negative and one for its positive parts, so this
            // emphasizes both, as hovering its name in the legend does
            chart.dispatchAction({ type: 'highlight', seriesName: p.seriesName });
            // The tooltip was already drawn for this mouse move, so redraw it
            chart.dispatchAction({
              type: 'showTip', x: p.event.offsetX, y: p.event.offsetY
            });
          });

          chart.on('mouseout', 'series', function(p) {
            hovered = null;
            chart.dispatchAction({ type: 'downplay', seriesName: p.seriesName });
          });
        }
      ", data = list(group = group, series = as.list(ids)))
  }
  
  # The end of the title for each choice of the main group dropdown and of the
  # subgroup dropdown or, in stack mode, of the type
  if (!is.null(title)) {
    name_of <- \(label) RawData$name[match(label, RawData$nameLabel)]
    ends <- if (stack) {
      unique(paths[, .(main, second = as.character(typeLabel))])[, end := fifelse(
        main == "Összesen", second, paste0(name_of(main), ", ", second)
      )]
    } else {
      unique(CategoryPaths[, .(main, second = sub)])[, end := fifelse(
        second == "Összesen", name_of(main),
        paste0(name_of(main), ", ", name_of(second))
      )]
    }
  }
  
  # The title, if any, with room for it above the plot, and room for the legend
  # below it: ECharts puts the legend at the bottom, and wraps it into more lines
  # when the chart is too narrow for one (as on phones), but only leaves room for
  # one, so the others would cover the horizontal axis
  chart <- chart |>
    htmlwidgets::onRender("
      function(el, x, data) {
        var chart = echarts.getInstanceByDom(el);
        var main = document.getElementById(data.mainId);
        // The subgroup dropdown or, in stack mode, the radio buttons of the type
        var second = document.getElementById(data.secondId);
        var download = document.getElementById(data.downloadId);
        // The height of the chart, and the room above and below the plot without
        // the title and with a legend of one line
        var option = chart.getOption(), height = el.clientHeight;
        var gridTop = option.grid[0].top, gridBottom = option.grid[0].bottom;
        var context = document.createElement('canvas').getContext('2d');

        // ECharts could wrap the title too, but wouldn't tell into how many
        // lines, which decides how much room the title needs
        function wrap(text, width) {
          return text.split(' ').reduce(function(lines, word) {
            var last = lines[lines.length - 1];
            if (last && context.measureText(last + ' ' + word).width <= width) {
              lines[lines.length - 1] = last + ' ' + word;
            } else {
              lines.push(word);
            }
            return lines;
          }, []);
        }

        // How much higher the legend is than its first line (its items are all of
        // the same height)
        function legendExtra() {
          var model = chart.getModel().getComponent('legend');
          var view = model && chart.getViewOfComponentModel(model);
          var items = view && view.getContentGroup(), first = items && items.childAt(0);
          return first ?
            Math.round(items.getBoundingRect().height - first.getBoundingRect().height) : 0;
        }

        function update() {
          // ECharts lays out the legend for the width it has, which htmlwidgets
          // may not have updated yet when the window was resized
          if (chart.getWidth() !== el.clientWidth) {
            chart.resize({ width: el.clientWidth, height: el.clientHeight });
          }
          var legendRoom = legendExtra(), titleRoom = 0;
          var options = { grid: { bottom: gridBottom + legendRoom } };
          var end = data.title && (data.ends[main.value] || {})[second.tagName === 'SELECT' ?
            second.value : second.querySelector('input:checked').value];
          // Unless the chart has no title, or the dropdowns aren't filled yet
          if (end) {
            // Smaller on phones, where the title takes several lines anyway
            var fontSize = el.clientWidth < 500 ? 14 : 18, lineHeight = fontSize + 6;
            context.font = 'bold ' + fontSize + 'px ' + option.textStyle.fontFamily;
            // Clear of the download button in the top right corner, by as much as
            // the title is from the left edge
            var right = download.getBoundingClientRect().left - el.getBoundingClientRect().left;
            var lines = wrap(data.title + ': ' + end, right - 20);
            titleRoom = lines.length * lineHeight;
            options.title = {
              id: 'category', text: lines.join('\\n'), left: 10, top: 5,
              textStyle: { fontSize: fontSize, fontWeight: 'bold', lineHeight: lineHeight }
            };
            options.grid.top = gridTop + titleRoom;
          }
          chart.setOption(options);
          // The chart grows by the room for the two, so that the plot keeps its
          // size. (The size is given explicitly, as ECharts would otherwise keep
          // using the one htmlwidgets last gave it when the window was resized)
          el.style.height = height + titleRoom + legendRoom + 'px';
          chart.resize({ width: el.clientWidth, height: el.clientHeight });
        }

        main.addEventListener('change', update);
        second.addEventListener('change', update);
        window.addEventListener('resize', update);
        // The legend needs its room even before the dropdowns are filled
        update();
      }
    ", data = list(
      title = title, mainId = filter_ids[2],
      secondId = filter_ids[if (stack) 4 else 3], downloadId = download_id,
      ends = if (!is.null(title)) {
        lapply(split(setNames(ends$end, ends$second), ends$main), as.list)
      }
    ))
  
  htmltools::tagList(
    filters,
    add_download_menu(chart, unit, id = download_id,
                      choice_id = if (length(var) > 1) var_id,
                      download_axis_name = download_axis_name)
  )
}
```

# Bevezetés

Az ország mindenkori költségvetésének összeállítása nagyon egyszerű feladat, ugyanis mindössze két eleme szokta vita tárgyát képezni: a bevételei és a kiadásai. Jelen weboldal ez utóbbival foglalkozik.

A költségvetés kiadásai az állampolgárok oldaláról nézve juttatásokat, állam által ellátott funkciókat, állam által biztosított szolgáltatásokat jelentenek, így ilyenből a többség általában többet lát kívánatosnak. Nincs értelme azt a kérdést feltenni, hogy "Ön több pénzt adna-e az egészségügynek?", mert erre kivétel nélkül mindenki azt fogja válaszolni, hogy igen, persze, naná. A probléma ott kezdődik, hogy pontosan ugyanezt válaszolnák arra a kérdésre, hogy több pénzt adna-e az oktatásra, hogy többet szánna-e a nyugdíjakra, hogy jobban támogatná-e a gazdákat, hogy több jusson-e a közlekedés fejlesztésére...

Tehát a célszerű kérdés, amit fel kell tenni, szerintem így hangzik: van 100 pengőnk, amit elkölthetünk, kérjük, *ossza szét* a különböző funkciók között! Mennyit adna az egészségügynek? Mennyit az oktatásra? Mennyit a nyugdíjakra? Mennyit a gazdák támogatására? Mennyit a közlekedés fejlesztésére? Bármennyire is bugyután hangzik a dolog, szerintem már ez hatalmas előrelépés az előbbi típusú kérdésekhez képest, mert *rákényszeríti* a válaszadót, hogy szembesüljön azzal, hogy ha valakinek többet ad, akkor másnak *muszáj* kevesebbet. Ez azért is jó, mert elejét veszi azoknak a válaszoknak, hogy "nem kéne lopni!!" -- persze, tényleg nem kéne, de ha ezt megszüntetjük, és ettől több pénzt oszthatunk is el (most tegyük félre azt a kérdést, hogy ez megvalósítható-e ilyen egyszerűen), *attól még* igaz marad az, hogy ha valahol többet költünk, akkor máshol muszáj kevesebbet. Ezért kell azt kérdezni, hogy milyen *arányban* adna az egészségügynek; legyen most ez a konkrét példa.

A másik, szorosan idekapcsolódó probléma, amikor nem ahhoz viszonyítják az elköltött pénzt, mint ami kívánatos lenne, hanem a múltbeli értékekhez: több pénzt szán a kormány az egészségügyre, mint 1/5/10/20/stb. évvel ezelőtt? (Ez különösen akkor szokott élesen felmerülni, ha 1/5/10/20/stb. évvel ezelőtt még egy másik kormány volt.) A probléma az, hogy ennek a kérdésnek semmi értelme nincsen ebben a formában, kezdve azzal, hogy a 20 évvel ezelőtti forint nem ugyanaz, mint a mai forint (2005-ben 173 forint volt egy kilogramm fehér kenyér), tehát bár *látszólag* mindkettő forintban van mérve, ez valójában két *különböző* mértékegység... olyan, mintha azt kérdeznék, hogy több-e 20 kilogramm, mint 10 amper. A másik probléma ezzel az, hogy a kormány *preferenciáit* nem az fejezi ki, hogy mennyi pénzt szán az egészségügyre, hanem az, hogy a mindenre összesen szánt pénz mekkora *hányadát* szánja az egészségügyre. Persze, hogy ma több pénzt költ egészségügyre, mint 20 évvel ezelőtt, de ma több pénzt költ *minden másra* is, tehát ebből -- ha valaki ilyen módon szeretné mérni -- nem derül ki, hogy "mennyire fontos" a kormány számára az egészségügy.

A gazdaság egy elképesztően (de nem használhatatlanságig) leegyszerűsített modellje a következő: valamennyi értéket megtermelünk $\rightarrow$ ennek valamekkora hányadát az állam elszedi (adók, járulékok) $\rightarrow$ ezt esetleg kiegészíti hitelfelvétellel (költségvetési hiány) $\rightarrow$ az ilyen módon megszerzett (elszedett + hitelként felvett) pénz valamekkora részét az egészségügynek adja. Ha tehát valaki azt kérdezi, hogy hogyan juthatna több az egészségügyre, akkor a válasz kiolvasható ebből: *vagy* több értéket kell termelni, *vagy* nagyobb arányban kell az államnak a termelt értékből beszedni, *vagy* több hitelt kell felvenni, *vagy* a megszerzett pénzből nagyobb arányban kell az egészségügynek adni (vagy ezek valamilyen kombinációja). Most nekünk nem annyira fontos, de egyébként az egész közgazdaságtan alapproblémája épp az, hogy ezek nem egyszeri, önmagukban álló döntések, hanem az egész rendszer visszahat saját magára: ha *most* nagyon sok pénzt szedek be, akkor az lecsökkentheti, hogy *később* mennyi kerül megtermelésre, ha jól allokálom a pénzeket, akkor később nagyobb lehet a növekedés stb.

Ez a weboldal a fentiekben kíván segítséget adni: megadja a költségvetés különböző területekre költött kiadásait, de megadja hozzá azokat a további információkat, számításokat is, amik segítik a fenti csapdák elkerülését és a valós kép összeállítását. Filozofikusabb értelemben a célom az információkhoz való demokratikus hozzáférés elősegítése volt, hogy ezek az adatok mindenki számára elérhetőek legyenek, mégpedig értelmezhető formában (hiszen itt a megfelelő értelmezés majdnem olyan fontos, mint a nyers adatokhoz való hozzáférés). Ahol lehet, vizualizációkat alkalmaztam, mert a megfelelő ábrák sokkal könnyebbé teszik egy számtenger megértését.

Bízom benne, hogy ilyen módon hozzájárul ez a weboldal a múltbeli adatok és a jelen helyzet jobb megértéséhez, ezen keresztül pedig segíti a jövőre vonatkozó viták színvonalának emelését is.

Az oldal megvalósításához kiindulópont, hogy rendelkezzünk a költségvetések múltbeli adataival. Ez nem teljesen nyilvánvaló kérdés, ezért egy külön [hobbiprojekt keretében](https://github.com/ferenci-tamas/magyar-koltsegvetes-adatbazis) töltöttem le a múltbeli költségvetések adatait; ott elolvasható az összes ezzel kapcsolatos részlet, valamint megtalálható egy adatbázisa is a magyar költségvetéseknek 1949-től napjainkig. A most felhasznált adatok 2001-től, illetve, bizonyos esetekben, 1995-től érhetőek el, egészen 2027-ig.

# Honnan szerezzünk ehhez adatot?

Az, hogy az állam mennyi pénzt szán az egészségügyre, a mindenkori költségvetésből olvasható ki, hiszen az épp azt tartalmazza (többek között), hogy az állam mire mennyi pénzt szán. A dolog azonban ennél több szempontból is bonyolultabb. Az első probléma, hogy a költségvetésben a kiadások nem funkciók -- egészségügy, oktatás, nyugdíj stb. -- szerint vannak csoportosítva, hanem intézményrendszer szerint. Ez elég nagy probléma, mert ugyanazon funkcióhoz tartozó kiadás számos helyen megjelenhet (a Honvédkórház a Honvédelmi Minisztérium fejezetében fog szerepelni, az allergia elleni védekezés egy része az agrárminisztérium fejezetében, a rehabilitáció a szociális minisztériumnál és így tovább). Elvileg tehát végig kellene olvasni -- és egyesével besorolni -- mind a sok ezer sort; a jó hír, hogy ezt a költségvetés készítői megteszik helyettünk, így születik meg a funkcionális kiadásokat tartalmazó tábla. Ez lesz az, amire szükségünk van! (Vagy, ha még pontosabbak akarunk lenni, a konszolidált funkcionális kiadásokat kell használnunk a mostani célunk érdekében. A konszolidálás azt jelenti, hogy ha az államháztartás egyik szerve egy másiknak pénzt küld, akkor az nem jelenik meg az előbbinél kiadásként, az utóbbinál pedig bevételként, hiszen az államháztartás egészét tekintve egy ilyen mozgás neutrális.)

További nehézség ennek kapcsán, hogy a gyakorlatban két *különböző* funkcionális osztályozási rendszer is [használatban van](https://www.allamkincstar.gov.hu/pfile/file?path=/Koltsegvetes/Kozponti_alrendszer_-_Merlegek/funkcionalis-merlegek/Allamhaztartasi_funkcionalis_bontas_szerinti_anyagok/Modszertani_leiras_az_allamhaztartas_funkcionalis_kiadasaihoz.docx&inline=true): egy hazai és egy nemzetközileg egységes, az ún. [COFOG-rendszer](https://www.ksh.hu/cofog_menu). A kettő szerencsére nagyjából kompatibilis egymással (a megfeleltetéseket a lenti ábrák és elemzések tartalmazni fogják, ezeket beépítettem). Mindenesetre azt el kell mondani, hogy ha a költségvetések hazai adatait nézzük, ott a besorolás a magyar rendszer szerinti lesz, viszont ha a nemzetközi adatszolgáltatások számára készülő statisztikákból [kérjük le](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/gov_10a_exp/default/table?lang=en) a kiadási adatokat, az a COFOG-rendszer szerinti lesz.

A második probléma, hogy valójában a költségvetésnek több állapota van:

- Az eredeti előirányzat: amennyit eredetileg terveztek.
- A módosított előirányzat: a tervezet menet közben módosítható (akár már az első benyújtás során, még mielőtt törvény lenne belőle, akár a már törvényként megjelent költségvetés is módosítható).
- A teljesítés: az utólagos visszatekintés, hogy mennyi lett a tényleges költés (szemben az előzőekkel, amik mind tervezett értékek). Ezt az ún. zárszámadás tartalmazza.

Szigorúan véve nekünk a teljesítés a fontos (hiszen ez mondja meg, hogy mennyi lett a *tényleges* költés), de azért érdekes kérdés lehet az eredeti előirányzatot is megnézni, hiszen ez meg arról mond valamit, hogy milyen minőségű volt a költségvetés tervezése, vagy milyen, előre nem látható események történtek. A nemzetközi adatszolgáltatás csak a teljesítésről szól, nem az előirányzatról.

A harmadik problémakör az, hogy milyen szemléletű adatokról beszélünk: a költségvetések kapcsán létezik pénzforgalmi szemléletű és eredményszemléletű érték. A pénzforgalmi szemlélet azt jelenti, hogy minden gazdasági eseményt, legyen az akár kiadás, akár bevétel, arra az időpontra könyvelünk le, amikor a hozzá tartozó pénz fizikailag gazdát cserél, tehát megérkezik a bevételünk vagy kifizetjük a kiadásunkat, nem pedig akkor, amikor az esemény megtörténik. Ez utóbbi az eredményszemlélet. A különbség megértéséhez nem kell országban gondolkoznunk: mondjuk egy vállalkozó elvégez és kiszámláz egy munkát aznapi teljesítéssel, ekkor eredményszemléletben arra a napra kellene könyvelni -- de hogy a pénz mikor érkezik meg fizikailag, az teljesen más kérdés, lehet, hogy a vevő készpénzben rögtön kifizeti, lehet, hogy 30 napra fizet átutalással, lehet, hogy 90 napra. Pénzforgalmi szemléletben arra a dátumra könyveljük, amikor a pénz megérkezik, ha aznap, akkor aznapra (ez esetben nincs különbség az eredményszemlélethez képest), de ha 90 nap múlva kapjuk meg, akkor 90 nappal későbbi dátumra. Vagy fordítva: ki kellene fizetnünk a februári gázszámlát, de késedelembe esünk -- ez a kiadás eredményszemléletben mindenképp februári, de pénzforgalmi szemléletben akkori, amikor végül is kifizetjük. A pénzforgalmi szemlélet előnye, hogy sokkal egyszerűbb, hamarabb meghatározható, hátránya, hogy igazából nem a valós folyamatokról ad képet (hiszen a mi munkánk leírására aligha jó az a mutató, ami attól is függ, hogy a vevőnk mennyit késik a fizetéssel). Amit tudni kell, hogy a költségvetés mellékleteiben közölt számok pénzforgalmi szemléletűek, a nemzetközi adatközlésben szereplők viszont eredményszemléletűek.
